statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ is quoted at 29,257.50 and 29,257.75, up 151.75 to 152.00 points or 0.52% on the 29,105.75 settle, after printing a fourth consecutive higher overnight high at 29,266.00 and holding within about 8 points of it. Repeated extension while trading near a session extreme is the amplifier this measure watches, and it has now persisted across four hours, which carries Tail up one point to 15. The counter-evidence keeps the reading well inside the low band. The entire overnight range is 29,017.00 to 29,266.00, roughly 249 points or 0.86%, and the regional cash session moved the other way: the Nikkei fell 0.9%, the Kospi 2.7% and MSCI Asia ex-Japan 0.5%. An overnight bid in NQ that Asian cash equities decline to confirm is a divergence, not the aligned one-way structure this measure is built to detect. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%, the 10-year is near 4.704% and the 2-year near 4.25% with both little changed, and oil is lower with WTI near $85 and Brent $92.08 after the announced Iran sanctions campaign. Tail sits at 15 with Stress at 45, holding the mapped state below the block threshold.
recommendation: Descriptive only. The observation that carries this hour is that the overnight extension sequence has continued for a fourth hour: NQ printed 29,168.25, then 29,197.00, then 29,225.00, and has now traded 29,266.00 while sitting within roughly 8 points of that high. Extension, brief pause, then a fresh high is the shape this measure treats as Tail-relevant, which is why Tail is carried up to 15 rather than allowed to decay. Three considerations hold the reading inside the low band. The amplitude is small: 249 points across the whole overnight session is about 0.86%, so the directional efficiency is operating on a narrow range and each leg has been a slow grind rather than an impulse. The cross-asset set is not confirming: VIX is at 14.89 after a 6.0% decline, the 2-year and 10-year yields are effectively unchanged near 4.25% and 4.704%, and oil is lower rather than gapping, with Brent at $92.08 despite the Iran sanctions campaign. And the regional evidence actively conflicts, with Japanese and Korean cash indices lower while NQ futures extended, which is the opposite of the aligned amplifier stack this measure requires before Tail rises materially. Today's US calendar carries no high-impact release, so conditional risk concentrates in the narrow window spanning the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z medium-impact cluster. Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods print, followed by Nvidia's results after that day's close, sit beyond this horizon and are carried as Stress rather than Tail.
headline: NQ extends to a fourth consecutive overnight high at 29,266 and holds within 8 points of it, but Asian cash indices fall, VIX sits at 14.89 and yields are unchanged; Tail 15 and Stress 45 into a US session with no high-impact release
body:
The decisive observation this hour is that the overnight extension sequence is intact and has lengthened. Investing.com shows NQ at 29,257.50, up 151.75 points or 0.52%, and Yahoo Finance shows 29,257.75, up 152.00 points, both on the 29,105.75 settle. The overnight band has widened to 29,017.00-29,266.00, and the 29,266.00 high is the fourth successive higher extreme after 29,168.25, 29,197.00 and 29,225.00 in the three preceding hours. Price is sitting in the top few percent of that band. Repeated extension combined with holding near the extreme is exactly the structure this measure treats as evidence that retracements are becoming shallow, so Tail is carried up from 14 to 15.

What prevents that from becoming a larger reading is amplitude and, more importantly, an absence of confirmation. A 249-point overnight range is about 0.86%, which is unremarkable, and each leg higher has taken roughly an hour rather than arriving as an impulse. The regional session moved the other way: MSCI Asia ex-Japan fell 0.5%, Japan's Nikkei 0.9% and South Korea's Kospi 2.7%, while the Hang Seng was flat and the ASX 200 rose 0.44%. A futures bid that Asian cash equities decline to follow is a divergence rather than the aligned, one-way path this measure is built to detect, and the advance itself is a partial repair of Monday's chip-led decline rather than a breakout: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,995.38, down 0.17%, near the bottom of its 29,971.92-30,195.72 range and about 2.5% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high.

The cross-asset set is calm to de-escalating. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0% from 15.84, having traded as low as 14.77. Treasury yields are close to unchanged after reporting that the Treasury may fund expanded debt buybacks, with the 10-year at 4.704% and the 2-year at 4.25%. Oil is lower rather than gapping: WTI is near $85 and Brent $92.08, both down more than 2% in the prior session after Treasury Secretary Bessent announced a sanctions campaign aimed at severing Iran's economic links, and shipments continue to move through the Strait of Hormuz. Monday's equity weakness was concentrated and identifiable rather than systemic, with Nvidia down about 2.9% for a seventh consecutive decline, Micron down 5.8%, Broadcom 2.6% and AMD 3.5%, on reports that Nvidia told customers AI server prices will rise more than 15% early next year on memory costs. Shared Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 06:20Z and treated as delayed supporting evidence only, is consistent: index futures modestly higher, VIX futures slightly lower, Treasury futures marginally softer, and a latest-session semiconductor complex in which all seven tracked names were lower with a mean change of -3.0%.

The conditional path holds inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 15 on the observed fourth overnight high, holds 15 at the European cash open because that clock-hour produced the largest reading of the preceding 24, then steps down through the European morning to a floor of 12. It rebuilds from 12:00Z as Fed Barkin and the weekly ADP print arrive, reaches 17 at 13:00Z for Case-Shiller and the 13:30Z cash open, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z where CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed index all land thirty minutes into cash trade. That peak remains below the block threshold because every US release today is medium impact and, on this calibration, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and reduce Confidence before they raise Tail. The overnight hours then fall back to 11 before drifting up to 15 by the end of the horizon as Wednesday's macro cluster and Nvidia's results come into view. Options are pricing about a 5.4% post-earnings move in Nvidia against a 7.4% twelve-quarter average, a comparatively contained expectation for the largest index constituent.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 06:00Z on 24 August with Tail 12 and Stress 46 in a normal mode. Its first structural peak came immediately after, at 07:00Z, where the European cash open produced Tail 19 with Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; that faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z, holding an 11 to 13 band through the European morning. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, which mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That peak decayed immediately, to 13 by 15:00Z and into single digits from 17:00Z onward as the US afternoon mean-reverted, running a 7 to 10 Tail band with Stress easing from 46 to 42. The overnight hours since have held a 9 to 13 band with Stress steady near 45 to 47, and the final two slots carried Tail 13 and then 14 in a trend-up mode as the overnight extension sequence developed.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 15 on the observed fourth consecutive overnight high and holds 15 at 07:00Z for the European cash open, the same clock-hour that produced the largest reading of the preceding 24. It then steps down through the European morning, 14 and then 13, to a floor of 12 at 10:00Z and 11:00Z, the calendar-empty part of the day. The series rebuilds to 14 at 12:00Z for the Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 17 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the cash open follows at 13:30Z, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z for the CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. That is the highest conditional reading of the horizon and it still sits below the block threshold, because today's US calendar carries no high-impact release and no post-event price path can be observed in advance. It decays to 16 and then 14 through the US morning, holds 13 to 14 across the afternoon, the 17:00Z two-year auction and the power hour, and falls to 11 after the cash close. The overnight stretch runs 11 to 12 before drifting to 13, 14 and 15 in the final three slots as Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods cluster, and Nvidia's results after that day's close, come into view. Stress traces the same shape one band higher, from 43 to 45 overnight to a 56 peak at 14:00Z and back to 52 at the horizon's end, while Confidence decays from 87 to 68 with distance from observed evidence. The narrow danger window is 13:30Z to 14:30Z, spanning the cash open and the medium-impact release cluster.
